articles.title: New Hallcon Contract Raises Wages, Improves Safety
articles.content_excerpt: On October 12, members of UE Locals 155, 977, 1077, 1177, and 1477 voted overwhelmingly to ratify a new four-year national collective bargaining agreement with their employer, Hallcon Inc. Base wages will increase between 11 and 25 percent over the duration of the contract. In the first year, most wages will increase between five and 10 percent. Hallcon is one of three main companies hired by the Class I freight railroads to transport rail crews within and between rail yards. Some UE members work as yard drivers, whose work is shifted and generally occurs within the confines and surroundings of a railyard. articles.title: To Feed the Hungry: The Merit of Charity
articles.author: Red Fault -- Austin DSA
articles.content_excerpt: By Asanti M. To recount the history of the human struggle against hunger is to see a true virtue birthed from necessity in its most basic form. From time immemorial cooperation precluded death; community cemented life; and collaboration rose as the principal weapon against hunger. To stave off the constant assault on our mortality, collective structures arose from collective needs. Both calculated and spontaneous efforts set in motion the systematic destruction of our innate enemy and laid the foundation for a solidarity rooted in a visceral understanding of the human condition. Rather than eliminate hunger, contemporary modes of societal organization produce social structures that justify material dispossession. articles.author: Groundwork Towards a Socialist Future
articles.source: Building Up: The Groundwork DSA Blog - Groundwork: Towards a Socialist Future
articles.content_excerpt: Why Chicago DSA Should Not Endorse Brandon Johnson Author: Chicago Groundwork Brandon Johnson is seeking Chicago DSA’s endorsement after a politically fraught first term. Soon the chapter will have to weigh in on if we will lend support to Mayor Johnson and what that support looks like. This question is not an easy one, as Brandon has been a key champion of many legislative priorities for Chicago DSA. Still, endorsing or recommending Brandon runs the risk of tying ourselves to a deeply unpopular incumbent and a failed model of progressive governance, all the while the DSA model is proving itself across the country. articles.title: Guglielmo Carchedi Was a Pathbreaking Marxist Economist
articles.author: Joseph Choonara
articles.content_excerpt: In October, the radical left lost Guglielmo Carchedi — “Mino” to his friends and comrades — who died in his sleep at the age of eighty-five. He was one of the great Marxist thinkers of our times. I first met him in London a few years after the economic meltdown of 2007–9, at a conference I organized for the journal International Socialism to explore the dynamics of that crisis. He spoke patiently and calmly, setting out his views with authority and an unwavering confidence in the power of Marxist theory. I heard him many more times over the next few years, always speaking with the same measured style. articles.title: Democrats Did Their Best Bernie Impression in the Midterms
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: The 2026 midterms saw historic gains for socialists and progressives. So, perhaps unsurprisingly, the Democratic Party’s corporate wing is hurriedly spinning the result as a victory for centrists and “moderates.” Largely lost in this is the way that the Left has transformed what it actually means to run as a Democratic moderate or a centrist. Because looking at this year’s campaigns, there is no doubt that even the most uninspiring “moderate” candidates were taking several pages — whole chapters, really — from the books of Bernie Sanders, Zohran Mamdani, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. articles.title: Five Things Socialists In Congress Should Do
articles.author: Will S.
articles.content_excerpt: Congress is about to boast more socialists than ever before. DSA seems poised to double or triple our Congressional slate in 2028 and 2030, but we actually say very little about what our federal representatives are supposed to do with their positions. Most of the discussion around our Socialists in Office, at all levels, is about passing legislation, but we need to acknowledge that right now we don’t even have the numbers or the organization to stop the priorities of our enemies in both parties, like tax cuts or more oil drilling, let alone to enact Medicare for All. We of course want to win non-reformist reforms to weaken capital and boost workers’ ability to fight. But to get there, we’ll need to go through a phase of growth, experimentation, and probably getting our asses kicked a bit.

articles.title: Possible Love Is a Cinematic Masterpiece About Class
articles.author: Kap Seol
articles.content_excerpt: Possible Love is yet another masterpiece that South Korean director Lee Chang-dong has brought to us, after an eight-year hiatus since his last film Burning (2018). Unlike his younger Korean peers, such as Bong Joon-ho ( Parasite ) or Park Chan-wook ( Old Boy and No Other Choice ), Lee, now seventy-two, has often found himself confined to the independent film scene outside South Korea, where he has usually enjoyed modest commercial success. Deeply rooted in humanity and class relations, Lee’s films deserve a wider audience beyond the ranks of art house aficionados (including Barack Obama, who named Burning among his favorite movies of 2018). articles.title: US Government Bureaucracy Is Designed to Punish the Poor
articles.author: Kelly McKowen
articles.content_excerpt: For several years, I lived in Norway and enjoyed the privileges associated with membership in Folketrygden , or the National Insurance Scheme. One privilege that I still think about often is the relative frictionlessness of interacting with the Norwegian government. Seeing a doctor, for example, was effortless, and once my low annual deductible (as of 2026, ~$300) was paid, all testing and treatment for the year was covered without my involvement or input. My taxes were — without my prompting — prepared for me and sent for my amendment and approval. There was never anything to amend, of course. articles.title: Eugene Debs’s Life Speaks to Today’s Socialist Movement
articles.author: Nelson Lichtenstein
articles.content_excerpt: Shawn Gude’s splendid new biography of Gilded Age Socialist Eugene V. Debs could hardly have arrived at a more propitious moment. Perhaps as many as half of all young people tell pollsters they prefer socialism to capitalism.
